title: Formally smooth for an adic topology on the target
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$ an ideal. $S$ is *formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology* if the following lifting property holds: for every commutative ring $D$ with a ring map $R\to D$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, with quotient map $q:D\to D/J$, and every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $g:S\to D/J$ which is continuous for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology on $S$ and the discrete topology on $D/J$, i.e. $g(\mathfrak n^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$, there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:S\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$ (such an $f$ is again continuous: $f(\mathfrak n^k)\subseteq J$, so $f(\mathfrak n^{2k})=0$). (This is Stacks More on Algebra, Definition 07EB for $R$ discrete, $S$ with the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology and $D$ discrete, continuity of $g$ being Lemma 07E9; by Lemma 07EC(2) it is the same as the condition with $R$ given the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology for any ideal $\mathfrak m\subseteq R$ with $\varphi(\mathfrak m^e)\subseteq\mathfrak n$ for some $e$, which is Definition 07NI.)
